title: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2014 Measures No. 5) Bill 2014
short_title: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2014 Measures No. 5) Bill 2014

speeches.speaker: Laurie Ferguson
speeches.brief: Reported that the Human Rights Committee examined 12 bills, found nine required no further scrutiny, deferred one and identified two for further examination; it concluded that 10 of 12 matters concerning the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (2014 Budget Measures No. 2) Bill 2014 were compatible with human rights.

speeches.speaker: Chris Bowen
speeches.brief: Outlined Labor's support for abolishing the mature age tax offset and updating deductible gift recipients, but opposition to R&D and seafarer tax offset changes, citing a $620 million cut to the R&D tax concession and a $115 million cut to the CSIRO, while contrasting this with a Paid Parental Leave scheme that could pay up to $50,000 per birth.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Criticised the government's priorities, noting it gave superannuation tax cuts to the 20,000 wealthiest people in the system while reopening $1.1 billion in multinational tax loopholes, contrasted with Labor's closure of similar loopholes worth $5.3 billion while in government, and said the bill's thin capitalisation changes were welcome but only a fraction of what Labor had planned.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill's seafarer tax offset abolition, worth just $8 million net over the forward estimates, and its $620 million cut to the R&D tax offset, contrasting this with $111 million in CSIRO cuts and 20 per cent cuts to university funding, arguing the government was pursuing an anti-science agenda while protecting the wealthy from budget repair.

speeches.speaker: Tony Smith
speeches.brief: Supported the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment bills, highlighting integrity measures expected to raise about $755 million over four years, and championed the government's new one-page personalised tax receipt showing taxpayers where their money is spent, recalling that Australia's net government debt was last fully repaid on 'debt-free day' in April 2006.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Opposed abolishing the seafarers tax offset, explaining Labor introduced it in 2012 to level the playing field for Australian shipping against foreign competitors, providing a rebate worth 30 per cent of a seafarer's pay for employees who work at least 91 days a year on international voyages, and noting 99 per cent of Australia's exports and imports move by sea.
